symbols.name: OmegaV
symbols.type: indexed family of finite state spaces
symbols.def: Each \(\Omega_v\) is finite and has at least two elements.

symbols.name: I
symbols.def: \(\mathcal I(c)=1\) records that CI statement \(c\) holds and \(\mathcal I(c)=0\) records that it fails.

symbols.name: B
symbols.type: finite set of background edge orientations
symbols.def: \(\mathcal B\) contains the required and forbidden orientations supplied to discovery.

symbols.name: G
symbols.type: finite family of SA-MPDAGs and CPDAGs
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak G\) is supplied with checkable certificates that it represents every minimum-edge DAG I-map of \(\mathcal I\) respecting \(\mathcal B\).

symbols.name: CI1
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C_1(\mathcal I)\) contains every determinantal minor encoding a bit-one CI statement.

symbols.name: CI0
symbols.type: finite family of finite polynomial blocks
symbols.def: For each bit-zero statement \(c\), \(\mathcal C_0(\mathcal I,c)\) is its block of determinantal minors, at least one of which must be nonzero.

symbols.name: u
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak u=(V,(\Omega_v)_{v\in V},\mathcal I,\mathcal B,\mathfrak G,X,x,Y,p^{\circ})\) passes the checks in \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\).

symbols.name: D0
symbols.def: For a certified input \(\mathfrak u\), \(D_0\) is the first DAG in the nonempty family \(\mathfrak D\) under the supplied canonical graph order.

symbols.name: TDy
symbols.def: \(T_{D,y}(p)\) is the outcome-cell marginal of the DAG truncated factorization after \(do(X=x)\).

symbols.name: BDy
symbols.def: \(B_{D,y}\) is the reduced denominator of \(T_{D,y}\), with every uncancelled marginal factor recorded.

symbols.name: KI
symbols.def: \(K_{\mathcal I}=\sqrt[\mathbb R]{J_{\mathcal I}:s^{\infty}}\), interpreted as rational polynomials vanishing on the real saturated variety.

symbols.name: prec
symbols.def: \(\prec\) is graded reverse lexicographic order on \(\mathbb Q[p_z:z\in\Omega]\) under the fixed cell order.

symbols.name: NF
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{NF}_{\prec,K_{\mathcal I}}\) uses a fixed graded reverse lexicographic order \(\prec\) and a canonical reduced basis of \(K_{\mathcal I}\).

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: \(H\) is the maximum input coefficient bit length after encoding the oracle minors, graph certificates, positive rational feasibility witness, query, and signatures.

symbols.name: d
symbols.def: \(d\) is the maximum total degree among generators of \(J_{\mathcal I}\), the polynomial \(s\), and the signatures \(F_{D,y}\).

symbols.name: r
symbols.def: \(r\) is the number of generators in the fixed encoding of \(J_{\mathcal I}\) together with the exact-oracle inequality blocks.

symbols.name: c0
symbols.def: \(c_0\) is the universal constant fixed by the effective real-Nullstellensatz encoding.

symbols.name: Aatlas
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak A_{\mathcal I}\) denotes a finite library sought by recursively orienting oracle-inseparable edges, parameterizing the resulting positive rational DAG or forest charts, and checking pullbacks of intervention signatures.

symbols.name: Istar
symbols.def: \(\mathcal I_{\star}\) is the exact CI bit-vector induced by \(p_{\star}\).

symbols.name: Bstar
symbols.role: background knowledge in the strictness witness

symbols.name: Gstar
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak G_{\star}=\{D_A,D_B\}\), with the exhaustive \(543\)-DAG enumeration as its tied-minimum certificate.
symbols.role: certified tied family in the strictness witness

symbols.name: ustar
symbols.role: strictness instance against the sufficient graphical test

symbols.name: tau
symbols.def: \(\tau(p)=(T_{D_0,y}(p))_y\) for tables at which the fixed equality-branch circuit has positive recorded denominators.

symbols.name: tauhat
symbols.def: \(\widehat\tau_n=\tau(\widehat p_n)\) whenever the fixed certified circuit is defined at \(\widehat p_n\).

symbols.name: Sigmahat
symbols.role: plug-in covariance of the empirical table

standard.name: Strict positivity for discrete graphical models
Determinantal encoding of discrete conditional independence

assumptions.condition: \(\sum_{g\in\mathcal C_0(\mathcal I,c)}g(p)^2>0\) for every CI statement \(c\) with \(\mathcal I(c)=0\).

standard.name: Exact CI-oracle realization by nonvanishing minors

assumptions.condition: \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) are independent and identically distributed with law \(P\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}=\{p\in\mathbb R^{\Omega}: \sum_zp_z=1,\ p_z>0\ \forall z,\ g(p)=0\ \forall g\in\mathcal C_1(\mathcal I),\ \sum_{g\in\mathcal C_0(\mathcal I,c)}g(p)^2>0\ \forall c\text{ with }\mathcal I(c)=0\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak D\)
definitions.construction: Expand every supplied \(G\in\mathfrak G\) into its represented DAGs, verify acyclicity, \(\mathcal B\), and \(\operatorname{CI}(D)\subseteq\{c:\mathcal I(c)=1\}\), and verify the supplied lower-bound certificate that no admissible I-map has fewer edges; retain all ties in canonical order.

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak u\)
definitions.construction: Verify that \(\mathfrak D\) obtained from \(\mathfrak G\) is nonempty; verify every supplied graph and minimum-edge certificate; and verify by exact rational arithmetic that \(p^{\circ}\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^{\Omega}\). The accepted tuple is \(\mathfrak u=(V,(\Omega_v)_{v\in V},\mathcal I,\mathcal B,\mathfrak G,X,x,Y,p^{\circ})\).

definitions.name: \(T_{D,y}\)
definitions.construction: For each \(D\in\mathfrak D\), expand \(\sum_{v_{V\setminus(X\cup Y)}}\prod_{j\notin X}p(v_j\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_D(j)})\) at \(X=x\) and \(Y=y\), express each conditional probability as an observed-table marginal ratio, and reduce to \(T_{D,y}=A_{D,y}/B_{D,y}\) while recording every uncancelled denominator.

definitions.name: \(F_{D,y}\)
definitions.construction: \(F_{D,y}=A_{D,y}B_{D_0,y}-A_{D_0,y}B_{D,y}\) for every \(D\in\mathfrak D\) and outcome cell \(y\).

definitions.name: \(K_{\mathcal I}\)
definitions.construction: Form \(J_{\mathcal I}=\langle\mathcal C_1(\mathcal I),\sum_zp_z-1\rangle\), saturate by \(s=\prod_zp_z\prod_{D,y}B_{D,y}\), and take \(K_{\mathcal I}=\sqrt[\mathbb R]{J_{\mathcal I}:s^{\infty}}\) over rational polynomials with a fixed-order canonical basis.

definitions.name: \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\)
definitions.construction: \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}=2^{(H+1)(2d+2)^{2^{c_0(m+r)}}}\), with all sparse exponents expanded in unary in the checked identity representation.

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak A_{\mathcal I}\)
definitions.construction: Begin with oracle-inseparable edge orientations; recursively add rational conditional-table charts for compatible DAG and directed-forest submodels; on each chart clear denominators in the pullback of every \(F_{D,y}\); retain a chart when its rational open box realizes the full exact CI bit-vector.

definitions.name: \(\operatorname{SparseSIM\text{-}ID}\)
definitions.construction: Accept only a tuple certified by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), construct all \(T_{D,y}\), \(F_{D,y}\), and \(K_{\mathcal I}\), and compute \(\operatorname{NF}_{\prec,K_{\mathcal I}}(F_{D,y})\) in canonical order. If every normal form is zero, output the reference arithmetic circuit and real-Nullstellensatz plus saturation identities. Otherwise enumerate reduced rational tables of bit length at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\) in canonical order until one lies in \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) and has a nonzero failed signature, then output that table and the corresponding DAG pair.

definitions.name: \((\widehat\tau_n,\widehat V_n)\)
definitions.construction: For one fixed certified input on the equality branch, set \(\widehat\tau_n=(T_{D_0,y}(\widehat p_n))_y=\tau(\widehat p_n)\) on the event \(\min_{D,y}B_{D,y}(\widehat p_n)>0\), set \(\widehat\Sigma_n=\operatorname{diag}(\widehat p_n)-\widehat p_n\widehat p_n^{\mathsf T}\), and set \(\widehat V_n=J_{\tau}(\widehat p_n)\widehat\Sigma_nJ_{\tau}(\widehat p_n)^{\mathsf T}\). Set \(\widehat\tau_n=0\) and \(\widehat V_n=0\) off that event.

statements.statement: For every finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), every \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\), and every \(D\in\mathfrak D\), the law \(p\) is Markov to \(D\). Hence the intersection of the represented DAG Markov models with the exact oracle model is exactly \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\), and no graph-local Markov generator strengthens \(J_{\mathcal I}\) on this domain.
statements.justification: This reduction prevents the minimum-edge promise from being mistaken for extra observed-law equations.
statements.gap: Raskutti and Uhler define sparsest I-maps, but do not isolate the common-law model needed for cross-graph effects.
statements.consumer: The algebraic certificate generator can omit redundant graph-local minors and report a smaller verified ideal.

statements.statement: Theorem 1 (effect-specific rational-positive separation). For every finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), every \(D\in\mathfrak D\), and every outcome cell \(y\), if \(F_{D,y}\notin K_{\mathcal I}\), then there exists \(p^{\dagger}\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^{\Omega}\) whose reduced coordinate numerators and denominators have bit length at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\) such that \(F_{D,y}(p^{\dagger})\ne0\). Conversely, \(F_{D,y}\in K_{\mathcal I}\) implies \(T_{D,y}(p)=T_{D_0,y}(p)\) for every \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\).
statements.justification: This is the load-bearing bridge from an algebraic failed equality to a checkable statistical ambiguity table.
statements.gap: Garcia, Stillman, and Sturmfels provide saturated components and effective algebra decides real feasibility, but neither yields a rational positive exact-oracle point separating a graph-indexed intervention signature.
statements.consumer: A discovery package can certify nonidentification with a finite rational table that users can inspect and replay exactly.

statements.statement: Every zero normal form \(\operatorname{NF}_{\prec,K_{\mathcal I}}(F_{D,y})=0\) admits a real-Nullstellensatz identity and explicit saturation-membership identities whose expanded total degree, coefficient bit length, and term count are each at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\); deterministic exact verification is polynomial in the expanded certificate length.
statements.justification: A termination theorem is meaningful only when both branches carry finite, size-accounted certificates.
statements.gap: Existing effective real-algebraic bounds do not instantiate the complete expanded certificate contract for these rational causal circuits.
statements.consumer: Independent proof checkers can validate equality outputs without trusting the computer-algebra system that produced them.

statements.statement: Theorem 2 (SparseSIM-ID completeness). For every finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), under Theorem 1, \(\operatorname{SparseSIM\text{-}ID}\) terminates after at most \(2^{2m(B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1)}\) exact rational-table checks and returns exactly one of two mutually exclusive certificates: either one observable arithmetic circuit \(\tau=(T_{D_0,y})_y\) with identities proving \(T_{D,y}=T_{D_0,y}\) on \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) for every \(D,y\), or \((D_0,D,p^{\dagger})\) with \(p^{\dagger}\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^{\Omega}\) and \((T_{D,y}(p^{\dagger}))_y\ne(T_{D_0,y}(p^{\dagger}))_y\). The first branch occurs if and only if the intervention law is common to every represented DAG. On tied SA-MPDAG families this is a strict decision-theoretic tightening of Theorem 3.2 of Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo: every query passing their sufficient graphical test is on the equality branch, while every query failing that test is still decided by an equality certificate or a rational positive separator. When \(\mathfrak G\) is a singleton and \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) equals its full positive Markov model, the decision agrees with Perkovic's single-MPDAG criterion and generalized truncated factorization.
statements.justification: The theorem replaces arbitrary selection among tied sparsest graphs by an effect-complete common-functional-or-counterexample contract.
statements.gap: Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo prove only a sufficient simultaneous criterion; Perkovic is complete for one MPDAG rather than a tied family across MECs.
statements.consumer: Tetrad SP and causaldag or GSP all-ties output can report a common effect circuit or an exact ambiguity table instead of choosing one tied graph.

statements.statement: For \(V=\{1,2,3,4\}\) with binary \(\{-1,+1\}\) states, the tuple \(\mathfrak u_{\star}\) is accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\). The table \(p_{\star}\) has exactly the elementary CIs \(1\perp2\), \(1\perp2\mid\{3,4\}\), \(3\perp4\), and \(3\perp4\mid\{1,2\}\). Among all \(543\) labelled DAGs, exactly \(50\) are I-maps, and the unique four-edge minima are \(D_A\) and \(D_B\), which lie in distinct MECs. Their probabilities for \(Y_3=+1\) under \(do(Y_1=+1)\) are \(13/20\) and \(1/2\), respectively.
statements.justification: The finite instance proves that the target family is nonvacuous beyond one Markov equivalence class.
statements.gap: The examples in Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo motivate tied sparsest outputs but do not provide this binary rational exact-oracle enumeration certificate.
statements.consumer: Implementers obtain a unit test whose graph counts, oracle bits, and intervention gap are all checkable by exact arithmetic.

statements.statement: Corollary 1 (strictness relative to Teh--Sadeghi--Soo). For the certified input \(\mathfrak u_{\star}\) and query \(P_{Y_1=+1}(Y_3=+1)\), the sufficient graphical conditions of Theorem 3.2 of Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo are not satisfied, whereas \(\operatorname{SparseSIM\text{-}ID}\) returns a rational positive separator; the table \(p_{\star}\) is an explicit admissible separator with graphwise values \(13/20\) under \(D_A\) and \(1/2\) under \(D_B\). Hence SparseSIM-ID strictly tightens that sufficient-only test on certified tied-sparsest inputs by resolving at least one query on which it is undecided.
statements.justification: This finite corollary turns the comparator relation into an auditable strict inclusion rather than a prose promise.
statements.gap: Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo give a sufficient graphical criterion and leave necessity unresolved; this certified exact-oracle instance is outside their decided region but receives a checkable nonidentification certificate.
statements.consumer: A regression test for Tetrad SP and causaldag or GSP can verify that an undecided graphical case is reported as exact ambiguity rather than silently selecting a graph.

statements.statement: Theorem 3 (fixed-input plug-in inference). Fix one finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), fix its equality-branch circuit \(\tau\), and fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\). Every recorded denominator is positive at \(P\), so the rational circuit \(\tau\) is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(P\), the event defining \(\widehat\tau_n\) has probability tending to one, and \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau(P))\Rightarrow\mathcal N\left(0,J_{\tau}(P)\Sigma_PJ_{\tau}(P)^{\mathsf T}\right)\). Moreover, \(\widehat V_n\xrightarrow{P}J_{\tau}(P)\Sigma_PJ_{\tau}(P)^{\mathsf T}\). If \(\sigma_y^2>0\), then \(\widehat\tau_{n,y}\pm1.96\sqrt{\widehat V_{n,yy}/n}\) has limiting coverage \(0.95\) for \(P_x(Y=y)\).
statements.justification: A certified population functional should produce standard sampling inference without graphwise duplicate estimates.
statements.gap: Chang, Guo, and Malinsky handle data-driven graph selection by interval unions; this theorem instead gives pointwise plug-in inference for one fixed certified oracle, tied family, and arithmetic circuit.
statements.consumer: After a population or externally certified discovery analysis, practitioners can estimate the common intervention probability with one covariance calculation.

statements.statement: Open-ended Question 1. Can the rational-chart handle \(\mathfrak A_{\mathcal I}\) be constructed so that, for every finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\) and every \(F_{D,y}\notin K_{\mathcal I}\), some retained chart has a nonzero pullback of \(F_{D,y}\) on a rational open box realizing the exact oracle, with a chart count and grid denominator bounded by \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\); and can the bound be reduced to singly exponential when every minimum DAG has bounded treewidth?
statements.justification: This exposes the constructive graph-native content required to prove Theorem 1 without appealing to an unjustified density of rational points on arbitrary CI varieties.
statements.gap: Directed-forest CI ideals have tractable prime parameterizations, but no existing atlas is known to be effect-separating for all signatures induced by tied sparsest DAGs.
statements.consumer: A positive answer yields finite rational witness search and practical certificate bounds; a negative answer identifies the precise family on which SparseSIM-ID must return algebraic rather than rational witnesses.

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from one fixed strictly positive multinomial law \(P\) after one certified input and its equality-branch circuit have been fixed.
sampling_model.units: The observations \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) are independent draws in the finite cell space \(\Omega\).
sampling_model.treatment: The intervention \(do(X=x)\) is a causal query, not a randomized sampling arm.
sampling_model.overlap: Membership \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) gives positive cells and positive recorded marginal denominators at the fixed law.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no nonparametric nuisances; \(\widehat\tau_n=\tau(\widehat p_n)\) and \(\widehat V_n=J_{\tau}(\widehat p_n)\{\operatorname{diag}(\widehat p_n)-\widehat p_n\widehat p_n^{\mathsf T}\}J_{\tau}(\widehat p_n)^{\mathsf T}\) are computed from the fixed certified circuit.

estimand_functional: \(P_x(Y=y)=T_{D,y}(p)=A_{D,y}(p)/B_{D,y}(p)\) for every \(D\in\mathfrak D\) on the equality branch

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.2 gives a sufficient graphical condition for simultaneous identification over a finite SA-MPDAG family.
Theorem 3.6 gives a necessary-and-sufficient criterion and generalized truncated factorization for one MPDAG.
Theorem 8 identifies a DAG factorization component by saturation of local and global Markov ideals.
Theorem 3 minimally enumerates distinct intervention functionals represented by one MPDAG.
IDP is sound and complete for causal-effect identification from one PAG.
A discrete causal query under one specified model compiles to a sharp polynomial program with anytime-valid outer bounds.
Resampling CI statistics and unioning graphwise intervals yields asymptotically correct coverage for a fixed effect after PC discovery.
SP consistently recovers the true MEC under the sparsest Markov representation condition.

tldr: Observational discovery can return several non-Markov-equivalent graphs with the same minimum edge count, and selecting one of them can change \(P_x(Y)\). SparseSIM-ID accepts a certified input only after checking that the tied family is nonempty and that a supplied positive rational table realizes the exact CI oracle. It converts every represented DAG's truncated factorization into a rational observed-table circuit and, conditional on the effect-specific rational-positive separation theorem, returns either a common circuit with fixed-order real-radical certificates or a bounded-height rational ambiguity table. The certified four-binary-variable instance is a strict decision-theoretic improvement over the sufficient graphical test of Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo, and a pointwise multinomial delta method supplies inference for one fixed certified equality-branch circuit.

project_justification.gap: Existing simultaneous-identification theory gives sufficient graphical conditions but not a necessary common-law test or a positive rational failure witness for tied sparsest outputs.
project_justification.niche: Minimum-edge ties are a structured and operationally important family in which graph-local Markov constraints are redundant, so completeness turns on the narrower algebraic question of whether intervention signatures detect only statistically relevant components of the oracle CI variety.
project_justification.fill: The project restricts attention to checkably nonempty certified inputs, isolates and proves an effect-specific rational-positive separation theorem, packages it into an exhaustive certificate algorithm with explicit size bounds, proves strictness over the closest sufficient graphical test on a certified rational witness, and attaches fixed-input plug-in inference with an explicit sandwich covariance to the common circuit.

related_work: Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo (Proceedings of the 42nd ICML, 2025, Theorem 3.2 and Section 4.2) give the closest causal boundary: their SA-MPDAG criterion is sufficient, and their necessity discussion asks for one common density with unequal graphwise effects. Theorem 2 is a strict decision-theoretic tightening on certified tied-sparsest inputs because it decides every query, while Corollary 1 gives a positive rational instance on which their graphical test is undecided and SparseSIM-ID returns a separator. Perkovic (2020, Theorem 3.6) supplies the graph-specific bucket truncated factorization adapted here into rational observed-cell circuits. Garcia, Stillman, and Sturmfels (2005, Theorem 8) inform saturation by positive marginal factors, while Kahle, Rauh, and Sullivant (2017, Sections 3.1 and 3.3) explain why irrelevant CI components make positivity a separate issue. Raskutti and Uhler (2018) define the tied minimum-edge discovery target without an effect-aware output policy. Guo and Perkovic (2021, Theorem 3) inform effect quotienting within one MPDAG. Jaber, Zhang, and Bareinboim (2019, Section 4.2) inform the success-or-obstruction proof architecture for one PAG. Duarte et al. (2024) inform polynomial compilation and certified optimization. Chang, Guo, and Malinsky (2024) inform the distinction between discovery and estimation uncertainty; Theorem 3 is pointwise for one fixed certified population input and does not claim selection-aware validity.
technical_internal_limitation: Saturation by cells and denominators excludes components contained in their zero sets but does not impose the signs \(p_z>0\), and it does not enforce the nonvanishing blocks associated with zero bits of an exact CI oracle. Therefore \(F_{D,y}\notin K_{\mathcal I}\) is not by itself a statistical nonidentification certificate. Theorem 1 is the substantive claim that closes exactly this gap for intervention signatures generated by tied minimum-edge families. General rational-point density on arbitrary CI varieties is neither assumed nor claimed.
honest_scope: The exact CI oracle, background orientations, query, complete tied minimum-edge family, and a positive rational exact-oracle feasibility witness are fixed certified population inputs; empty graph families and unrealizable exact oracles are outside the accepted domain. Theorem 1 and the rational-atlas question are open and headline-bearing; real-radical computation, certificate checking, and the pointwise fixed-input delta method are supporting results. The four-variable certified table has minimum cell \(1/40\), exactly four elementary CIs, \(50\) I-map DAGs, exactly two four-edge minima in distinct MECs, and intervention probabilities \(13/20\) and \(1/2\). If rational-positive separation fails, a complete algebraic-number witness procedure remains possible but is outside the claimed theorem. When the candidate family is one MPDAG and the oracle model equals that graph's positive Markov model, Theorem 2 reduces to Perkovic's known criterion. Theorem 3 fixes one certified input and one interior law; it makes no uniform claim over changing circuits, and data-driven estimation of the CI oracle or sparsity ties requires separate selection-aware analysis.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction and Section 4.2 were read together with Theorem 3.2 and its proof in Appendix A, especially the common-density necessity obstruction on page 4 and the reweighting argument on pages 7--8.
seed_details.kernel: For a fixed exact finite CI oracle and its certified tied minimum-edge DAG family, characterize simultaneous identification by membership of every cross-multiplied intervention signature in the saturated real radical, and prove that every failed membership has a bounded-height strictly positive rational exact-oracle separator.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first new step after Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo is to replace their pairwise chain-graph sufficient comparison by an effect-specific density theorem connecting algebraic non-membership to the positive exact-oracle locus.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for simultaneous identification with positive rational CI witnesses and for sparsest-permutation effect ties found no theorem occupying this target--method pair; the closest algebraic literature studies CI varieties without cross-graph intervention signatures.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee may call the result immediate from real quantifier elimination; the rebuttal is that quantifier elimination yields real-algebraic feasibility, while the claimed rational exact-oracle witness and equality criterion from a fixed saturated real radical are precisely the unresolved effect-specific bridge.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The kernel is not a one-law witness: it is uniform over every certified finite tied-sparsest input, while the explicit four-variable law is retained only as a nonvacuity check.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction, Algorithm 1, Theorem 3 and its constructive Gaussian separation sketch on page 5, Corollary 1, the complexity discussion, and the conclusion on pages 7--8 were read.
seed_details.kernel: Partition tied minimum-edge DAGs from several MECs into maximal classes having the same intervention rational function on the common exact-oracle law, with one canonical algebraic normal form per class and output-sensitive delay.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is Guo and Perkovic's shortest-path orientation invariant: cross-MEC transitions require equality modulo a shared positive CI model rather than syntactic equality of formulas inside one MPDAG.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing effect-minimal enumeration with multiple MECs and CI-ideal normal forms found structural enumeration and within-MPDAG quotienting, but no cross-MEC common-law quotient.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may say this is Guo--Perkovic with more input graphs; the rebuttal is that their distinctness witness uses one Markov-equivalence class and does not decide identities created only by CIs shared across different MECs.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed names a computable quotient and a delay guarantee, rather than treating graph enumeration as the contribution.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction, canonical response-function construction, polynomial-program compilation, sharpness argument, Algorithm 1, and the branch-and-bound certificate discussion were read on pages 3--14 and 38--40.
seed_details.kernel: When common point identification fails, compute the sharp range and maximal pairwise disagreement of all graphwise intervention functionals over the strictly positive exact-oracle model, with certified outer bounds and multinomial uncertainty propagation.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed Autobounds step replaces one SCM's response-function parameterization by shared observed-cell variables, graph-indexed rational objectives, exact non-CI inequalities, and a common positivity domain.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for sharp bounds over several observationally compatible MECs found graphwise possible-effect enumeration and general single-model polynomial programs, but no shared-law cross-graph disagreement program.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may call this a direct Autobounds compilation; the rebuttal is that direct composition optimizes separate model laws and therefore misses the common-law coupling that defines simultaneous ambiguity.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The graph-native compatible-law domain, exact-oracle inequalities, and explicit disagreement objective prevent a generic LP relabeling.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction, Theorems 6 and 8 with their localization proofs on pages 8--11, and Proposition 19's positive-density argument on page 23 were read.
seed_details.kernel: Return a real-algebraic positive separator by quantifier elimination whenever a graphwise intervention signature differs on the common CI model.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step augments CI implicitization by graph-indexed truncated-factorization objectives and strict inequalities.
seed_details.destination_search: Effective real algebraic geometry already decides this feasibility problem in generic form.
seed_details.red_team: The cynical objection holds: once rational output is abandoned, generic real quantifier elimination supplies the decision theorem, leaving mainly a domain-specific compilation.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Dropped because the claimed advance would be supporting machinery rather than a theorem-level causal kernel.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction, the proper possibly causal path criterion, bucket decomposition, Theorem 3.6 and its proof architecture, and the final comparison to adjustment were read on pages 1--9.
seed_details.kernel: Give a necessary-and-sufficient simultaneous-identification criterion for arbitrary finite families of MPDAGs with semi-directed cycles.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step replaces the chain-component factorization used for SA-MPDAGs by Perkovic's partial-causal-order bucket factorization before comparing several graph classes.
seed_details.destination_search: The search confirmed complete single-MPDAG identification and complete single-PAG identification, but no simultaneous criterion for arbitrary MPDAG families.
seed_details.red_team: The novelty objection fails, but the seed is dropped because it simultaneously requires a new semi-directed-cycle calculus and a shared-law converse, with no bounded early-kill construction comparable to the sparsest-family test.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Dropped on feasibility rather than padded as a broader version of the selected kernel.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction, resampling and screening construction, Theorems 1--3 and their retention-event proofs on pages 6--10 and 18--24, and the limitations and permutation-method discussion on pages 16--17 were read.
seed_details.kernel: Derive a uniform limit law for a common rational effect under local-to-zero CI signals and local sparsity-score ties, using resampled graph retention and one pooled influence function.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step replaces coverage through inclusion of one valid graph and a union of intervals by stability of a certified common functional across all retained tied graphs.
seed_details.destination_search: The search found post-PC union inference and randomized graph-selection inference, but no pooled common-functional limit law for sparsest-permutation ties.
seed_details.red_team: The objection that the certificate removes selection is false near CI boundaries; nevertheless the seed is dropped because solving discovery nonregularity before establishing population completeness reverses the dependency order.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: This is a limit-law seed rather than a bare inference add-on, but it belongs after the selected population theorem.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction, maximum-cardinality-search enumeration, the MPDAG extension, the structural-Hamming-distance theorem, proofs, and conclusion were read on pages 1--8.
seed_details.kernel: Augment linear-delay local orientation updates with cached intervention normal forms so that consecutive outputs enumerate effect classes rather than DAGs.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step makes the traversal state remember a law-relative effect normal form, which is not invariant under the local graph moves alone.
seed_details.destination_search: No effect-aware linear-delay result was found, but normal-form computation can dominate graph delay exponentially.
seed_details.red_team: The referee objection that algebraic normalization destroys the claimed linear delay currently holds, so this seed is dropped in favor of the output-sensitive quotient without a premature linear bound.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Dropped rather than hiding certificate size outside the delay measure.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction, region decomposition, IDP algorithm, termination and soundness proof, failure-to-hedge construction, Theorems 3--5, and Conclusion were read on pages 1--8.
seed_details.kernel: For several PAGs, return a common functional or one observed law and two compatible latent-variable SCMs with different effects.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step must replace Jaber, Zhang, and Bareinboim's one-PAG hedge construction by a hedge pair whose induced observational law is shared by all candidate PAGs.
seed_details.destination_search: No multi-PAG shared-law completeness theorem was found, but latent-variable compatibility makes the common witness substantially harder than the causally sufficient sparsest-DAG case.
seed_details.red_team: The novelty rebuttal survives, but the proposed common latent law is unconstrained by the sparsest structure that supports the current constructive evidence.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Dropped because it expands both graph semantics and witness construction at once.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction, SP construction, SMR condition, consistency theorem and comparison with faithfulness on pages 1--5, together with the final simulation discussion, were read.
seed_details.kernel: Choose a smallest collection of intervention queries whose answers distinguish all effect classes among tied sparsest DAGs.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step turns the SP score's graph-recovery objective into a query-separation set-cover objective over tied outputs.
seed_details.destination_search: The search found active causal discovery and experiment-design literatures but no direct theorem for a minimum diagnostic query set over exact-oracle sparsest ties.
seed_details.red_team: The objection that this is a set-cover wrapper is persuasive unless interventions have new structural submodularity, for which the anchor provides no evidence.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Dropped because the named optimization object lacks a nontrivial causal optimality theorem.

adjacent_threads: Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo (2025), Theorem 3.2 and Section 4.2: a sufficient SA-MPDAG criterion and an explicit statement that necessity requires one density Markov to every candidate graph with unequal interventions.
Perkovic (2020), Theorem 3.6: the complete single-MPDAG proper-path criterion and bucket truncated factorization supply each graph-specific rational functional.

Garcia, Stillman, and Sturmfels (2005), Theorem 8: saturation identifies the distinguished factorization component away from marginal hyperplanes, but the paper also shows that algebraic and probabilistic loci can differ.

Kahle, Rauh, and Sullivant (2017), Sections 3.1 and 3.3, and Mohammadi (2023), Section 2: CI ideals may have statistically irrelevant components, and rational-point existence is not a generic corollary of real solvability.
literature_map.settled: Graph-specific identification, CI-minor encoding, saturation, real-radical membership, and real-algebraic feasibility are settled supporting tools.
literature_map.unoccupied_kernel: No located paper proves that a nonzero intervention signature for a tied minimum-edge exact-oracle family has a strictly positive rational exact-oracle witness, nor a common-functional-or-rational-table complete procedure.
literature_map.method_adapted: Adapt Perkovic's bucket truncated factorization into rational observed-cell circuits, Garcia--Stillman--Sturmfels localization into the common CI ideal, and Jaber--Zhang--Bareinboim's success-or-explicit-obstruction proof architecture.

adjacent_threads: Guo and Perkovic (2021), Theorem 3: shortest-path recursive orientation minimally separates functionals inside one MPDAG and constructs a shared Gaussian law only because all outputs are Markov equivalent.
Wienobst et al. (2023): DAGs in one MEC admit linear-delay enumeration and local transitions of bounded structural Hamming distance.
Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo (2025): several non-equivalent SA-MPDAGs can nevertheless share an effect under sufficient graphical conditions.
Garcia, Stillman, and Sturmfels (2005): canonical equality modulo observational constraints requires an ideal calculation rather than syntactic formula comparison.
literature_map.settled: Minimal effect enumeration within one MPDAG and graph enumeration within one MEC are settled.
literature_map.unoccupied_kernel: No located result computes maximal effect classes across distinct tied sparsest MECs modulo their common exact-oracle law.
literature_map.method_adapted: Retain Guo and Perkovic's query-relevant recursion but replace its formula-distinctness invariant by a cached fixed-order normal form modulo the positive common-law model.

adjacent_threads: Duarte et al. (2024): canonical finite SCMs compile a discrete query into a sharp polynomial program with anytime-valid outer bounds.
Guo and Perkovic (2021): graph-induced functionals can be quotiented before numerical evaluation, but only inside one MPDAG.
Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo (2025): simultaneous identification is binary and their failure region has no sharp disagreement magnitude.
Chang, Guo, and Malinsky (2024): multinomial or graphwise sampling uncertainty must be separated from discovery uncertainty.
literature_map.settled: Sharp polynomial bounds for one declared discrete causal model and finite lists of possible effects inside one MPDAG are settled.
literature_map.unoccupied_kernel: No located result optimizes several rational truncated factorizations over one shared strictly positive exact-CI law.
literature_map.method_adapted: Use Autobounds' auxiliary-variable polynomialization and branch-and-bound certificate, with one common observed table and graph-indexed causal objectives.
